newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CommBank underwrites A$515 mln Boral debt.
newsitem.headline: CommBank underwrites A$515 mln Boral debt.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia said on Thursday it is to arrange and underwrite A$515 million of bank debt to support the float of Boral Ltd's gas distribution business.
Boral announced plans in June to float its gas distribution business through a new company, Envestra Ltd.
The new company would purchase the gas network assets from Boral Energy Ltd for A$889 million, funded by bank debt, equity and capital indexed bonds, Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) said.
The A$515 million of bank debt includes A$160 million for capital expenditure and a A$10 million working capital facility.

"We believe the bank was successful because of our ability to underwrite the full debt requirement for a transaction of this size and our leadership position in the Australian infrastructure market, in line with our funding of major road, energy and water treatment infrastructure," Nick Johnson, CBA's head of business development, institutional banking said.

CBA said it had been involved with most of the major infrastructure deals in Australia, was the first bank to take equity in an infrastructure project, the first bank to accept patronage risk and had pioneered the market in infrastructure bonds. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
